Helm.ai reports $70 million in contracts as physical AI expands beyond cars

The 12-month commercial milestone spans automakers, Tier 1 suppliers and industrial automation companies, according to Helm.ai.

The Robot Report ↗8 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

A year of signed contracts

Helm.ai announced on October 8 that it signed $70 million in commercial contracts over a 12-month period. Customers include automakers, Tier 1 suppliers and industrial automation companies. The figure measures signed contracts, rather than new investment or fully recognized revenue. The company says it is progressing toward operating breakeven, not that it has already reached it.

Separating perception from action

The company’s unsupervised Deep Teaching approach learns environmental structure while separating perception from downstream planning and action. Management says this improves data efficiency and enables shared capabilities across cars, mining equipment and construction applications. Those efficiency advantages are company claims; the report does not include an independent comparative benchmark.

Different applications are at different stages

The platform spans L2–L4 automotive programs and heavy-equipment perception projects progressing toward production. Helm.ai also describes delivery-drone work and broader robotics ambitions, without publishing deployment counts by application. The contract total therefore does not establish that a corresponding fleet of fully autonomous robots is already commercially operating.
